transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-04-22
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lina (Redwood SE), Maya (Vectra Head of ML), Rafael (Vectra Platform Eng), Priya (Vectra Security)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. We've got Lina (SE) with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Maya: Hi, thanks. Doing good. Excited to learn more. We're just trying to understand how Redwood would fit into our stack.
[00:15] Lina: Great. Quick agenda - integration options (SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex), proxy/gateway patterns, rate limits/quotas, and what observability hooks you get. We'll also cover Dedicated and Private options briefly.
[00:28] Rafael: Sounds good. For context - our infra is GCP-based, we run services in a VPC, we use internal proxies for outbound traffic, and our ML infra runs on k8s. We use LangChain in a few products and LlamaIndex for semantic search-ish flows.
[00:44] Priya: From security side - we need SOC 2, SSO/SAML, audit logs, and KMS for key management. We'll want to understand data residency and whether you support VPC peering or private link.
[00:56] Lina: All right. For SDKs - we have official SDKs in Python, JS, and Go. They support streaming, structured outputs, function calling, and can integrate natively with LangChain and LlamaIndex. Quick note - sometimes in our docs 'LlamaIndex' appears as 'LamaIndex' in auto transcriptions, that's a doc typo we've been fixing.
[01:13] Maya: Nice. Does the LangChain adapter live in the SDK or is it a separate repo?
[01:18] Lina: We provide adapter examples and an official connector in our sample repos. The pattern is you can plug Redwood as the LLM provider in LangChain chains, same with LlamaIndex loaders. We also have a small wrapper that handles tokenization and output parsing so you get consistent structured responses.
[01:34] Rafael: About network - we operate behind a corporate proxy. What's the recommended pattern? Use your hosted API through our gateway, or run Redwood Private inside our VPC?
[01:44] Samir: It depends on your data and compliance needs. For low-friction pilots we recommend Hosted API behind a proxy - you'll configure egress rules and use our SDK's proxy settings. For stricter controls we offer Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private deployments with VPC peering or customer-managed networking.
[02:03] Priya: On Private - do you support customer KMS or HSM? We can't have keys outside our control for production.
[02:09] Lina: Yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. For Dedicated we also support bring-your-own-KMS for encrypt-at-rest. We'll follow up with exact provider docs (GCP KMS, AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault details in the security pack).
[02:25] Maya: Good. Rate limits - we have bursty traffic with peaks during business hours. How do quotas and rate limiting work? We don't want throttling to break user flows.
[02:36] Lina: We expose per-key rate limits and per-route quotas. With Dedicated you can get capacity reservations (throughput guarantees) and can set rate limit policies per-route. There's also a routing policy for graceful fallback to cheaper/fast models when capacity is constrained.
[02:52] Rafael: Does the SDK handle retry/backoff for transient 429s? We have background workers and also synchronous API calls.
[02:58] Lina: Yes, the SDK includes configurable retries, jittered backoff, and idempotency helpers. For synchronous needs we suggest a short timeout and client-side concurrency limits; for async you can use our streaming/webhook-based patterns.
[03:12] Maya: Observability - what telemetry do we get? We need token-level cost breakdowns for each request and per-route latency histograms.
[03:20] Samir: In Redwood Console you'll get token-level cost by request, per-model dashboards, traces integrated with OpenTelemetry, and per-route latency/p95 metrics. We can also push logs to your logging endpoint or export metrics to your Prometheus/Grafana stack.
[03:34] Priya: Audit logs - are they exportable? We need immutable logs for compliance.
[03:38] Lina: Yes, audit logs are exportable to your cloud storage or SIEM. Private/Dedicated deployments give you customer-controlled log retention and we support S3/GCS sinks.
[03:48] Rafael: For integration with LangChain, any gotchas? We use few custom prompt templates and chain-of-thought style prompts.
[03:55] Lina: A couple notes: we preserve streaming semantics which LangChain expects; we also provide a prompt templating helper that integrates with LangChain. For chain-of-thought, cost can be higher - we recommend using prefix/KV caching for repeated context and using quantized model variants on Dedicated to save cost.
[04:12] Maya: Quantization - do you manage model quantization or do we pick a quantized variant?
[04:17] Lina: We maintain a catalog of verified model variants (including int8, awq-ish configs). For Dedicated you can pin a specific quantized build. We also provide recommendations in Redwood Optimize to pick the right model/quant profile per workload.
[04:33] Maya: Great. On the proxy side - is there an example of running a gateway that handles multi-tenant routing and injects auth?
[04:42] Lina: Yes, we have a sample gateway that acts as a reverse proxy and token bucket rate limit middleware. It also handles service-to-service auth via mTLS. I can share the repo after the call - it's in the sample integrations.
[04:53] Rafael: That'd be helpful. For the pilot, we'd want to run some benchmarks - 95th p90 latency at a couple of token lengths and throughput numbers. Can Redwood run a benchmark from dedicated capacity to mimic our expected delta?
[05:06] Samir: Absolutely. We can spin up a small Dedicated pool for a benchmark, or run hosted tests against representative models. Lina will own the benchmark setup with you.
[05:16] Priya: Any data residency support? Our EU traffic needs to remain in EU regions.
[05:20] Lina: Hosted supports region selection - EU-only regions for data processing. Dedicated/Private can be provisioned in region-specific infra as well.
[05:29] Maya: Who are some references you have in our vertical? We're in telecom analytics, not a huge enterprise yet but enterprise-grade needs.
[05:36] Samir: We have references in payments and telecom; I'll share a one-pager. Apologies, that was 'Gamma Telecom' - our field reference list.
[05:43] Maya: No worries.
[05:45] [06:00] -- small crosstalk, someone on mute --
[06:05] Rafael: Regarding SDK auth - we use SSO for engineers. Can Redwood integrate with Okta SAML for token issuance or do we use API keys?
[06:15] Lina: For Hosted API we typically use API keys, but we also support SSO-provisioned API keys and SAML/SCIM provisioning for teams. For Private you can map to your IdP and use short-lived tokens with RBAC.
[06:29] Priya: RBAC granularity - can we control route-level permissions and who can create model rollouts?
[06:34] Lina: Yes, RBAC supports role definitions with permissions scoped to routes, model rollout privileges, and billing-related ops.
[06:43] Maya: Cost - rough order of magnitude? We need to present to finance.
[06:47] Samir: I'll send the pricing sheet, but ballpark - hosted per-token pricing with discounts at volume; Dedicated has a reserved monthly commit plus lower per-token unit. Exact numbers depend on model selection and throughput.
[06:59] Rafael: One more technical - KV cache and prefix caching for chat workloads. Do you support sharing KV cache across nodes for a sharded Dedicated pool?
[07:08] Lina: We have a distributed KV cache layer that supports sharded deployments. For low-latency chat we keep KV cache warm on the serving nodes; when you scale out we have cache-repopulation strategies to minimize cold-start latency.
[07:23] Maya: Are there any limitations with LangChain's async calling model?
[07:27] Lina: LangChain's async patterns map well to our streaming SDKs; main caveat is you should avoid long-poll synchronous blocking operations that tie up client threads. We have example patterns in the repo.
[07:40] Priya: From compliance - do you do penetration testing and pen test reports available?
[07:46] Samir: Yes, we have pen test summaries and SOC 2 Type II attestation. We'll include certs in the security pack.
[07:55] Maya: Next steps - we want a pilot to test integrations (LangChain + LlamaIndex), run benchmarks, and validate security posture. Timeline target is pilot kickoff by mid-May.
[08:05] Samir: That works. Lina, can you lead the tech setup?
[08:09] Lina: Absolutely. I'll share the sample repos: SDK examples, LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, and the proxy/gateway example. I'll also schedule a setup call with Rafael for the benchmark.
[08:20] Rafael: For the benchmark data - we'll share a redacted prompt set and traffic profile.
[08:24] Priya: I'll send the security questionnaire and network diagram.
[08:28] Samir: Great, I'll follow up with pricing and refs. Any other Qs?
[08:34] Maya: One small thing - do you support direct Prometheus metrics or is it via exporter?
[08:39] Lina: We export metrics to Prometheus via an exporter; we can also push metrics to your managed Prometheus with a pull endpoint.
[08:48] Maya: Perfect.

-- Recap / Close --
[08:55] Samir: Recap: Send pricing and refs (Samir), share SDK and LangChain/LlamaIndex samples + proxy example (Lina), Priya sends security pack items, Rafael shares traffic profile. Schedule benchmark deep-dive week of May 4. Pilot target mid-May. We'll also share Dedicated vs Hosted decision matrix.
[09:12] Maya: Thanks everyone. Look forward to the next steps.
[09:16] Lina: Thanks, bye.
[09:18] End of call

Notes about transcript quality: auto transcription had a few entity errors - 'LamaIndex' for LlamaIndex, 'Gamma Telecom' mentioned as demo reference. Some timestamps approximate.
